en kirke.explanation: "En kirke" means "a church". To say you go to church, use "i kirke" (in church) after the verb: "Vi går i kirke i morgen" (We are going to church tomorrow).

en kirkegård.explanation: "En kirkegård" means "a cemetery". It is built from "en kirke" (a church) and "en gård" (a yard), so it literally means "churchyard". In another word, "gård" means "a farm": "en gård på landet" (a farm in the country).

en kirurg.explanation: "En kirurg" means "a surgeon". The subject itself is called "kirurgi" (surgery). To name a surgeon who works on hearts, add the body part in front: "en hjertekirurg" (a heart surgeon).

en kiste.explanation: "En kiste" means "a chest", as in a large box with a lid. In a different meaning, it is a coffin: "Kisten blev båret ud af kirken" (The coffin was carried out of the church).

en kiwi.explanation: "En kiwi" means "a kiwi", as in the fruit. The plural is "kiwier", not "kiwis": "Jeg køber tre kiwier" (I buy three kiwis).

en kjole.explanation: "En kjole" means "a dress". To name the kind of dress, put a word in front of it: "en festkjole" (a party dress) and "en sommerkjole" (a summer dress).

en klage.explanation: "En klage" means "a complaint". The matching verb is "at klage over" (to complain about). To say you want to complain about food, say: "Jeg vil klage over maden" (I want to complain about the food).

en klapvogn.explanation: "En klapvogn" means "a stroller". To say you push it, use "at skubbe" (to push): "Jeg skubber klapvognen" (I push the stroller). For a baby who lies down, use "en barnevogn" (a baby carriage): "Babyen sover i barnevognen" (The baby sleeps in the baby carriage).

en klasse.explanation: "En klasse" means "a class", as in a group of pupils. To say which school year a child is in, put a number in front: "Hun går i 2. klasse" (She is in second grade).

en klassekammerat.explanation: "En klassekammerat" means "a classmate". It is built from "en klasse" (a class) and "en kammerat" (a pal). The word "kammerat" also appears in "en holdkammerat" (a teammate).

en klasselærer.explanation: "En klasselærer" means "a class teacher". It is built from "en klasse" (a class) and "en lærer" (a teacher).

en klassificering.explanation: "En klassificering" means "a classification". It comes from the verb "at klassificere" (to classify).

en klassiker.explanation: "En klassiker" means "a classic". To say a dish has always been on a restaurant's menu, say: "en klassiker på menuen" (a classic on the menu). For classical music, use the adjective "klassisk" (classical): "Jeg lytter til klassisk musik" (I listen to classical music).

en klat.explanation: "En klat" means "a dollop / blob". To name what the blob is made of, put the material straight after "klat", with no word for "of": "en klat maling" (a blob of paint).

en klejne.explanation: "En klejne" means "a Christmas cruller". It is a traditional Danish Christmas pastry: a twisted strip of dough fried in fat.

en klemme.explanation: "En klemme" means "a clothespin / clip". In a different meaning, to say someone is stuck in a tight spot, use "at sidde i klemme" (to be in a bind): "Jeg sidder i klemme" (I am in a bind).

en klient.explanation: "En klient" means "a client". In a shop or café, the word for a person who buys is "en kunde" (a customer): "Kunden betaler ved kassen" (The customer pays at the register).

en klinik.explanation: "En klinik" means "a clinic". To say someone is in a hospital, use "et sygehus" or "et hospital" (both mean a hospital): "Min mor ligger på sygehuset" (My mother is in the hospital).

en klipning.explanation: "En klipning" means "a haircut". To say you are getting one, use "at få" (to get): "Jeg skal have en klipning i morgen" (I am getting a haircut tomorrow). For the style itself, use "en frisure" (a hairstyle): "Hun har en ny frisure" (She has a new hairstyle).

en klippe.explanation: "En klippe" means "a cliff / rock". Do not mix it up with the verb "at klippe" (to cut): "Jeg klipper papir" (I cut paper).

en klit.explanation: "En klit" means "a sand dune". Denmark has tall sand dunes along the west coast of Jutland.

en klo.explanation: "En klo" means "a claw". To say someone falls into another person's power, use "at falde i kløerne på" (to fall into the clutches of): "Musen faldt i kløerne på katten" (The mouse fell into the clutches of the cat).

en klode.explanation: "En klode" means "a planet". The form "kloden" means "the Earth", as in "rundt om kloden" (around the globe). For a planet such as Mars, the ordinary word is "en planet": "Mars er en planet" (Mars is a planet).

en klods.explanation: "En klods" means "a block". The word "klods" is also the end of "legoklodser" (Lego bricks).

en klokke.explanation: "En klokke" means "a bell". When you ask what time it is, you use the form "klokken" (the bell): "Hvad er klokken?" (What time is it?)

en klovn.explanation: "En klovn" means "a clown". In a different meaning, it describes a person who acts foolishly: "Stop med at være en klovn" (Stop being a clown).

en klub.explanation: "En klub" means "a club", as in a group of people. To say you join one, use "at melde sig ind i" (to join): "Jeg melder mig ind i en klub" (I join a club).

en klud.explanation: "En klud" means "a cloth / rag". For drying plates, use "et viskestykke" (a dish towel): "Jeg tørrer tallerkenen med et viskestykke" (I dry the plate with a dish towel).

en klump.explanation: "En klump" means "a lump". To say a smooth mix has lumps in it, use the plural: "Der er klumper i saucen" (There are lumps in the sauce).

en kløver.explanation: "En kløver" means "a clover". To name a clover with four leaves, use "en firkløver" (a four-leaf clover). In a card game, "kløver" is also the suit of clubs: "Hvem har kløver es?" (Who has the ace of clubs?)

en knage.explanation: "En knage" means "a coat hook". To tell someone to hang a coat up, say: "Hæng jakken på knagen" (Hang the jacket on the hook).

en knallert.explanation: "En knallert" means "a moped". In Denmark, a moped with a top speed of 45 km/h is called "en knallert 45".

en knap.explanation: "En knap" means "a button". In a different meaning, the word "knap" without "en" means "barely": "Jeg har knap nok tid" (I barely have time).

en knibe.explanation: "I knibe" means "in a fix". To say someone gets into trouble, use "komme i knibe" (to get into trouble): "Han kommer i knibe, hvis han glemmer det" (He will be in trouble if he forgets it). To say you help someone out, use "hjælpe en ud af knibe" (to help someone out of a fix): "Jeg hjælper dig ud af knibe" (I will help you out of a fix).

en kniv.explanation: "En kniv" means "a knife". To say you eat with cutlery, put "kniv" before "gaffel" (fork): "Jeg spiser med kniv og gaffel" (I eat with a knife and fork).

en knivspids.explanation: "En knivspids" means "a pinch", as in a small amount. It is built from "en kniv" (a knife) and "en spids" (a tip). To name what the pinch is made of, put the ingredient straight after it, with no word for "of": "en knivspids kanel" (a pinch of cinnamon).

en knogle.explanation: "En knogle" means "a bone". To say someone has broken a bone, use "at brække" (to break): "Han har brækket en knogle i foden" (He has broken a bone in his foot).

en knop.explanation: "En knop" means "a bud". Do not mix it up with "en knap" (a button): "Der mangler en knap på jakken" (A button is missing on the jacket).

en knude.explanation: "En knude" means "a knot". To say your hair is tangled, use: "en knude i håret" (a knot in the hair). In a different meaning, a tight spot in a muscle is also a knot: "en knude i nakken" (a knot in the neck).

en knægt.explanation: "En knægt" means "a lad / kid". For a boy, the ordinary word is "en dreng" (a boy): "Drengen leger i haven" (The boy plays in the garden).

en ko.explanation: "En ko" means "a cow". The plural is "køer", not "koer": "Der står tre køer på marken" (Three cows stand in the field).

en koalition.explanation: "En koalition" means "a coalition". To say groups join together in one, use "at danne" (to form): "De tre grupper dannede en koalition" (The three groups formed a coalition).

en kobling.explanation: "En kobling" means "a clutch", as in the pedal of a car. In a different meaning, it is the coupling that joins two train cars: "en kobling mellem to togvogne" (a coupling between two train cars).

en kode.explanation: "En kode" means "a code". In a different meaning, it is computer code: "Han skriver kode" (He writes code).

en kofanger.explanation: "En kofanger" means "a bumper". It is built from "en ko" (a cow) and "at fange" (to catch), so it literally means "cow catcher".

en kogeplade.explanation: "En kogeplade" means "a hotplate". It is built from "at koge" (to boil, to cook) and "en plade" (a plate).

en kogle.explanation: "En kogle" means "a pine cone". To name the tree, put it in front: "en grankogle" (a spruce cone).

en kogning.explanation: "En kogning" means "a boiling". It comes from the verb "at koge" (to boil). To tell someone to bring a pot to a boil, say: "Bring det i kog" (Bring it to a boil).

en kok.explanation: "En kok" means "a chef". Do not mix it up with "at koge" (to boil): "Jeg koger æg" (I boil eggs).

en kokkeelev.explanation: "En kokkeelev" means "a chef apprentice". It is built from "en kok" (a cook) and "en elev" (a pupil). The word "elev" also appears in "en skoleelev" (a school pupil).

en koldskål.explanation: "En koldskål" means "a cold buttermilk dessert". It is a Danish dish eaten with small crisp cookies called "kammerjunkere".

en kollega.explanation: "En kollega" means "a colleague". The plural is "kolleger", not "kollegaer": "Mine kolleger spiser frokost sammen" (My colleagues eat lunch together).

en kolonihave.explanation: "En kolonihave" means "an allotment garden". In Denmark, it is a small rented plot with a little house on it, in an area with many other plots. The word is built from "en koloni" (a colony) and "en have" (a garden).

en kombination.explanation: "En kombination" means "a combination". In a different meaning, it is the set of numbers that opens a lock: "Jeg glemte kombinationen" (I forgot the combination).

en komedie.explanation: "En komedie" means "a comedy". For a sad story, use "en tragedie" (a tragedy): "Filmen er en tragedie" (The film is a tragedy).

en komet.explanation: "En komet" means "a comet". To name the most famous comet, say "Halleys komet" (Halley's comet).

en komiker.explanation: "En komiker" means "a comedian". To name a comedian who performs stand-up, use "en stand-up-komiker" (a stand-up comedian).

en kommando.explanation: "En kommando" means "a command". To say something happens when someone gives the order, use "på kommando" (on command): "Soldaterne marcherer på kommando" (The soldiers march on command). In a different meaning, it is a line you type in a computer: "Skriv kommandoen i terminalen" (Type the command in the terminal).

en kommandør.explanation: "En kommandør" means "a commander". It comes from "en kommando" (a command).

en kommentar.explanation: "En kommentar" means "a comment". The action is "at kommentere" (to comment). To say you comment on a video, say: "Jeg kommenterer videoen" (I comment on the video).

en kommentator.explanation: "En kommentator" means "a commentator". It comes from the verb "at kommentere" (to comment).

en kommissær.explanation: "En kommissær" means "a commissioner". To name a member of the European Commission, use "en EU-kommissær" (an EU commissioner).

en kommode.explanation: "En kommode" means "a chest of drawers". Danish spells it with a "k" where English "commode" has a "c".

en kommune.explanation: "En kommune" means "a municipality". Denmark is divided into 98 municipalities.

en komponist.explanation: "En komponist" means "a composer". The ending "-ist" marks a person in other words: "en pianist" (a pianist) and "en turist" (a tourist).

en koncentration.explanation: "En koncentration" means "a concentration". In a different meaning, it is how much of a substance is in a mix: "koncentrationen af salt i vandet" (the concentration of salt in the water).

en koncert.explanation: "En koncert" means "a concert". To say you go to a concert, leave out "en": "Vi går til koncert i aften" (We are going to a concert tonight).

en kondicykel.explanation: "En kondicykel" means "an exercise bike". The start "kondi" is short for "kondition" (fitness): "Jeg har god kondition" (I have good stamina).

en kondolence.explanation: "En kondolence" means "a condolence". The verb is "at kondolere" (to offer condolences): "Jeg kondolerer" (My condolences).

en kone.explanation: "En kone" means "a wife". For a woman in general, use "en kvinde" (a woman): "Kvinden står ved bussen" (The woman stands at the bus).

en konfirmation.explanation: "En konfirmation" means "a confirmation". In Denmark, young people are confirmed around age 14, and the party after it is called "en konfirmationsfest" (a confirmation party).

en konflikt.explanation: "En konflikt" means "a conflict". To say people solve one, use "at løse" (to solve): "De løste konflikten" (They solved the conflict).

en konge.explanation: "En konge" means "a king". Denmark's official name is "Kongeriget Danmark" (the Kingdom of Denmark).

en konklusion.explanation: "En konklusion" means "a conclusion". In a different meaning, it is the last part of a report: "Læs konklusionen først" (Read the conclusion first).

en konkurrence.explanation: "En konkurrence" means "a competition". The verb is "at konkurrere" (to compete). To say someone won it, use "at vinde" (to win): "Hun vandt konkurrencen" (She won the competition).

en konkurrent.explanation: "En konkurrent" means "a competitor". It comes from the verb "at konkurrere" (to compete).

en konsekvens.explanation: "En konsekvens" means "a consequence". To say something will have consequences, use "at få konsekvenser" (to have consequences): "Det vil få konsekvenser" (There will be consequences). Do not mix it up with the adjective "konsekvent" (consistent): "Hun er altid konsekvent" (She is always consistent).

en konsistens.explanation: "En konsistens" means "a texture". Do not use it for English "consistency" in the sense of doing the same thing each time. For that, use "konsekvent" (consistent): "Hun er altid konsekvent" (She is always consistent).

en konsonant.explanation: "En konsonant" means "a consonant". To name the other kind of letter, use "en vokal" (a vowel): "E er en vokal" (E is a vowel).

en konsulent.explanation: "En konsulent" means "a consultant". It comes from the verb "at konsultere" (to consult).

en kontakt.explanation: "En kontakt" means "a contact / a switch". When you talk about a person you know who can help you, it means "a contact": "Jeg har en kontakt i banken" (I have a contact at the bank). When you talk about the thing you press to turn on a light, it means "a switch": "Kontakten er ved døren" (The switch is by the door).

en kontaktlinse.explanation: "En kontaktlinse" means "a contact lens". It is built from "en kontakt" (a contact) and "en linse" (a lens).

en kontaktløs betaling.explanation: "En kontaktløs betaling" means "a contactless payment". The ending "-løs" means "without": "kontaktløs" is "without contact", and "håbløs" (hopeless) uses the same ending.

en kontaktperson.explanation: "En kontaktperson" means "a contact person". To say a man or a woman is the contact person, the word stays the same: "Han er vores kontaktperson" (He is our contact person) and "Hun er vores kontaktperson" (She is our contact person).

en kontekst.explanation: "En kontekst" means "a context". To say words are used in the wrong setting, use "taget ud af kontekst" (taken out of context): "Ordene er taget ud af kontekst" (The words are taken out of context).

en konto.explanation: "En konto" means "an account", as in an account at a bank. To say you open one, use "at oprette" (to open, to set up): "Jeg vil gerne oprette en konto" (I would like to open an account).

en kontorassistent.explanation: "En kontorassistent" means "an office assistant". It is built from "et kontor" (an office) and "en assistent" (an assistant).

en kontorplads.explanation: "En kontorplads" means "a workspace". For a whole room, use "et kontor" (an office): "Jeg har mit eget kontor" (I have my own office).

en kontorstol.explanation: "En kontorstol" means "an office chair". It is built from "et kontor" (an office) and "en stol" (a chair). The word "stol" also appears in "en spisestol" (a dining chair).

en kontrakt.explanation: "En kontrakt" means "a contract". For an agreement that is only spoken, use "en aftale" (an agreement): "Vi har en mundtlig aftale" (We have a spoken agreement).

en kontrast.explanation: "En kontrast" means "a contrast". To compare two things, use "i kontrast til" (in contrast to): "I kontrast til sommeren er vinteren mørk" (In contrast to the summer, the winter is dark).

en kontrol.explanation: "En kontrol" means "a check / control". When the police or a border guard stops you to look at your papers, it means "a check": "Der er kontrol ved grænsen" (There is a check at the border). When you talk about power over something, it means "control": "Han har kontrol over bilen" (He has control of the car).

en kontrolafgift.explanation: "En kontrolafgift" means "a penalty fare". It is built from "en kontrol" (a check) and "en afgift" (a fee). To say you must pay it, say: "Jeg skal betale en kontrolafgift" (I have to pay a penalty fare).

en koordinat.explanation: "En koordinat" means "a coordinate". To ask for the place of something, use the plural: "Send mig koordinaterne til stedet" (Send me the coordinates for the place).

en kop.explanation: "En kop" means "a cup". To name what is in the cup, put the drink straight after "kop", with no word for "of": "en kop te" (a cup of tea).

en kopi.explanation: "En kopi" means "a copy". To ask someone to make one, use "at lave" (to make): "Kan du lave en kopi af nøglen?" (Can you make a copy of the key?)

en kopimaskine.explanation: "En kopimaskine" means "a copier". It is built from "en kopi" (a copy) and "en maskine" (a machine). The word "maskine" also appears in "en vaskemaskine" (a washing machine).

en korporal.explanation: "En korporal" means "a corporal". To use the rank with a name, put it before the name: "korporal Hansen" (Corporal Hansen).

en kosmetolog.explanation: "En kosmetolog" means "a beautician". For someone who cuts hair, use "en frisør" (a hairdresser): "Frisøren klipper mit hår" (The hairdresser cuts my hair).

en kost.explanation: "En kost" means "a broom". In a different meaning, the word "kost" without "en" means "diet": "sund kost" (a healthy diet). For cleaning a floor with electricity, use "en støvsuger" (a vacuum cleaner): "Støvsugeren står i skabet" (The vacuum cleaner is in the cupboard).
